methods.label: Find B's distance between meetings
methods.explanation:
Measure distance in laps. Between consecutive meetings, the runners' distances add to exactly one lap because they run in opposite directions.

In the \(15\) seconds between meetings, \(A\) runs
\[
\frac{15}{40}=\frac38
\]
of a lap. Therefore \(B\) runs
\[
1-\frac38=\frac58
\]
of a lap in the same time. At this pace, \(B\)'s time for one whole lap is
\[
15\div\frac58
=15\cdot\frac85
=24\text{ seconds}.
\]
The answer is \(24\) seconds, choice B.
